claims.text: Existing monitoring frameworks report current coverage and cannot anticipate its deterioration.
Under country-grouped cross-validation, a persistence baseline achieves an AUC of 0.968, dominating rank-order discrimination.
Inclusion of conflict and climate covariates improves model calibration, reducing Brier score from 0.196 to 0.190.
Equity weighting narrows the equal-opportunity gap across income groups by 41.5%.
Temporal attribution identifies the urban–rural gap as the fastest-rising predictor of future water insecurity.
Only 40.5% of countries are projected to achieve SDG 6.1.
No low-income country is on track to achieve SDG 6.1.

methodologies.name: Conflict-augmented, equity-weighted machine learning framework
methodologies.description: Predicts whether safely managed drinking water coverage will fall below 50% five years ahead using 15 socioeconomic, service-coverage, conflict, and climate features.

limitations.text: Current monitoring frameworks only report current coverage and cannot anticipate its deterioration.
A persistence baseline dominates rank-order discrimination (AUC = 0.968) over machine learning models under country-grouped cross-validation.
